title: The Magnetic Fields of the Dusty Nuclei and Molecular Outflows of Arp 220
question: What are the magnetic field properties (configuration and strength) and their role in the dusty nuclei and molecular outflows of the Ultra-Luminous Infrared Galaxy Arp 220?

data.angular_resolution: 0.24'' x 0.16'' (PA -31 deg) for continuum; 0.34'' x 0.24'' (PA -35 deg) for CO(3-2)
data.sensitivity: 99 uJy/beam (Stokes I continuum), 18.9 uJy/beam (Stokes Q and U continuum), 0.27 mJy/beam (CO(3-2) median rms across all Stokes and channels)

what.value: Sub-mm/mm continuum fluxes in the spectral range of 100-691 GHz within apertures of 0.1''-0.5''

evidence.quote: We estimate that both nuclei are nearly optically thin at $345.8$ GHz after obtaining a flux dependence of $\sim\nu^{2.4}$ in the spectral range of $100-691$ GHz using fluxes within apertures of $0.1\ensuremath{''}-0.5\ensuremath{''}$ from (cite: Sakamoto2008; wilson2014; Scoville2016; Martin2016).

what.value: CO(3-2) molecular masses of 10^6 M_sun and 10^7 M_sun and volumes in the blue and redshifted outflows, and outflow velocity ranges

evidence.quote: We measure a velocity dispersion of $\sim220$ km s$^{-1}$ in the polarized molecular outflows and take the CO(3-2) molecular masses of $10^{6}$ M$_{\odot}$ and $10^{7}$ M$_{\odot}$ within a volume of $90\times50\times50$ and $121\times50\times50$ pc$^{3}$ (length$\times$width$\times$depth; assuming an axysymmetric outflow) in the blue and redshifted outflows, respectively, from (cite: Wheeler2020).

evidence.loc: The polarized CO(3-2) molecular outflow of Arp 220 W
evidence.quote: We show the integrated intensity of the CO(3-2) molecular outflows for each core, using the velocity ranges as in (cite: Wheeler2020), which reveals the known fast ($\sim500$ km s$^{-1}$) molecular outflows in both cores.

what.value: Literature magnetic field estimates (B_ISM, B_OH, B_min, B_SNR) in Arp 220

evidence.quote: Table notes: $^{a}$ B$_{\rm{eq}}$, B$_{\rm{OH}}$, B$_{\rm{Bmin}}$, and B$_{\rm{SNR}}$ are taken from (cite: McBride2014).

what.value: FIR B-field strength of M 82 (305+-5 uG) and B-SFR scaling factor B_0 = 128 uG M_sun^-0.34 yr^0.34

evidence.quote: Using the FIR B-field strength of M 82, $305\pm5\,\mu$G (cite: LR2021), the scaling factor is $B_{0} = 128\,\mu$G M$_{\odot}^{-0.34}$ yr $^{-0.34}$ (cite: LR2023).

what.value: Star formation rate within the outflow of Arp 220 (5 M_sun yr^-1)

evidence.quote: The SFR within the outflow of Arp 220 is 5 M$_{\odot}$ yr$^{-1}$ (cite: Perna2020).

recipe.goal: Self-calibrate and image full-Stokes dust continuum and CO(3-2) line cubes
recipe.method: Independent self-calibration of CO(3-2) line data and continuum windows; imaging continuum with Briggs robust = 0.5 and CO(3-2) by averaging 4 channels with natural weighting
key_parameters: robust = 0.5 for continuum; natural weighting and 4-channel averaging (13.5 km/s) for CO(3-2)

recipe.goal: Measure dust continuum and CO(3-2) line polarization and validate against instrumental polarization
recipe.method: Select pixels with PI/sigma_PI >= 4 (and I_CO/sigma_I_CO >= 140 for CO(3-2)), rotate dust polarization angles by 90 deg to obtain plane-of-sky B-field orientation, rotate CO(3-2) polarization angles by 90 deg based on offset from dust, and measure integrated quantities in elliptical apertures of 0.5'' x 0.6''
key_parameters: PI/sigma_PI >= 4; I_CO/sigma_I_CO >= 140; elliptical apertures 0.5'' x 0.6'' tilted at +25 deg (East) and -25 deg (West)
assumptions: Both nuclei are nearly optically thin at 345.8 GHz (nu^2.4 flux dependence); both dust and CO(3-2) trace the same dominant B-field component in the outflow so CO(3-2) polarization is perpendicular to B-field

recipe.goal: Estimate magnetic field strengths in the molecular outflows of Arp 220 W
recipe.method: Calculate B-field strengths using turbulent kinetic energy equipartition (B_eq), classical Davis-Chandrasekhar-Fermi (B_DCF), modified DCF for shear flows in outflows (B'_DCF), and SFR scaling (B_SFR), with uncertainties from bootstrapping 1,000 random iterations
key_parameters: sigma_CO = 220+-20 km/s; M_CO = 10^7 M_sun (red) and 10^6 M_sun (blue); V = 121x50x50 pc^3 (red) and 90x50x50 pc^3 (blue); U_0 = 500+-50 km/s (red) and 460+-50 km/s (blue); sigma_theta = 12+-5 deg (red) and 20+-10 deg (blue)
assumptions: Axisymmetric outflow volume; factor of 2 uncertainty in outflow molecular mass; dust and molecular gas are cospatially embedded in the same B-field of the outflow

Exact channel velocities (in LSRK or barycentric frame) corresponding to the 16 redshifted and 1 blueshifted CO(3-2) polarized channel maps

score_reason: The paper clearly states the ALMA project code, weighting schemes, beam sizes, noise levels, SNR cuts, aperture geometries, and the exact equations and input parameter values (Table 3) for the B-field calculations. However, the CASA calibration/self-calibration and tclean parameters are omitted, and there is a minor formula inconsistency in the text vs. Table 2 for B_eq.
rediscovery_reason: Single ALMA dataset (2023.1.00044.S) with well-defined target apertures, explicit SNR thresholds (PI/sigma_PI >= 4, I/sigma_I >= 140), and complete tabular inputs (Table 3) and outputs (Tables 1 and 2) for both polarimetric measurements and B-field strength derivations.
